identity.name: SCAN STEELS LTD.
identity.industry: Integrated Secondary Steel Producer with Captive Power & Downstream Value Addition

summary.oneLiner: Scan Steels is an Odisha-based integrated secondary steel producer leveraging captive power, backward integration, and its dominant SHRISHTII TMT brand to drive EBITDA margin expansion from 5.9% to 13.9% by FY31, with a three-phase capex plan to scale finished capacity to 7.5 LTPA and unlock Rs.575 Cr EBITDA potential. Its low net debt-to-equity (0.16x), disciplined working capital, and entrenched distribution channel de-risk volume-led growth in India’s infrastructure-driven steel upcycle.

one-line thesis: Scan Steels is an Odisha-based integrated secondary steel producer leveraging captive power, backward integration, and its dominant SHRISHTII TMT brand to drive EBITDA margin expansion from 5.9% to 13.9% by FY31, with a three-phase capex plan to scale finished capacity to 7.5 LTPA and unlock Rs.575 Cr EBITDA potential. Its low net debt-to-equity (0.16x), disciplined working capital, and entrenched distribution channel de-risk volume-led growth in India’s infrastructure-driven steel upcycle.
financial scorecard / credit view: X838 Cr revenue / X49 Cr EBITDA / X20 Cr PAT / X441 Cr net worth (FY26); CRISIL BBB+/Stable (Jul'25) - rationale: disciplined leverage, strong promoter backing, premium equity raise at 47% above CMP, and consistent profitability through cycle
guidance / outlook: Management estimates FY28 EBITDA at X145 Cr and FY31 EBITDA at X575 Cr; strategy centers on three themes: (1) Billet expansion to 3 LTPA by Sept'26, (2) Pipe/Galv plant (2 LTPA) by Q3FY28, (3) Greenfield pellet + DRI + 50 MW power by Q3FY31; no formal guidance on share price or revenue targets beyond FY31.
order book & pipeline: N/A (no explicit order book disclosed; demand visibility driven by ~99% direct TMT offtake via entrenched Odisha dealer network and infrastructure tailwinds)
segment / subsidiary detail: TMT Bars: 2.0 LTPA capacity, 82% util, branded SHRISHTII (Fe-500D/550D), Rs.43,430/ton realization; Sponge Iron: 1.5 LTPA, 84% util, 75% internally consumed; MS Billets: 2.0 LTPA, 81% util; Captive Power: 8 MW, 100% util; Pipe/Galv: 0 LTPA currently, 2 LTPA under construction; Pellet: 0 LTPA currently, 12 LTPA planned.
growth verticals / optionality: Bindals NCLT revival (1.0 LTPA billet + 12.5 MW power by Mar'2028) adds inorganic scale; captive pellet plant (12 LTPA) enables full upstream control; potential replication of Odisha model in other mineral-rich states; epoxy-coated TMT and structural steel offer higher-margin product extensions.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin: 5.9%; FY31 target: 13.9%; cost advantages: captive power (8 MW → 58 MW) reduces energy cost from ~₹6.8/kWh (grid) to ~₹4.0/kWh; low inbound logistics due to Odisha ore belt location; hot charging reduces billet reheat cost; brand premium of Rs.1,500–2,000/ton over unbranded local players; blended EBITDA/ton: ₹3,013 (FY26) → target ₹4,000+ (FY31)
capex / expansion: X850 Cr total allocation: Pellet Plant (X250 Cr), DRI Unit (X200 Cr), Billet/SMS (X80 Cr), Captive Power (X200 Cr), Land/Civil/Utilities (X40 Cr), WC/Contingency (X60 Cr); funded by X500 Cr fresh equity (59%) and X350 Cr internal accruals (41%); no term debt.
capital allocation: X500 Cr equity raise at ₹57.12/share (47% premium to CMP) to fund Theme 3; X350 Cr internal accruals reinvested; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on capex-driven capacity expansion, not shareholder returns; net debt-to-equity remains low at 0.16x (FY26) and targeted to fall to 0.04x by FY31.
risks & watch-items: Execution delays in Theme 3 (pellet, power, DRI) beyond Q3FY31; delays in Bindals revival beyond Mar'2028; iron ore/coal supply disruptions due to monsoon, mine strikes, or transport strikes; inflationary pressure on capex costs; regulatory delays in statutory clearances; competition from primary steelmakers if prices collapse; demand slowdown in infrastructure if government capex falters.
non-obvious takeaways: The company’s ~90-day raw material inventory buffer (not finished goods) is a strategic defense against Odisha’s frequent mine strikes, transporter disruptions, and monsoon-induced ore moisture spikes — a hidden operational moat that ensures continuity, unlike peers with leaner inventories.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
